newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soybean exports seen moderating after record.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soybean exports seen moderating after record.

text.p: U.S. soybean exports are expected to moderate soon after hitting record levels in November of 152 million bushels, the largest volume ever for a single month, the Agriculture Department said Thursday.
Climbing U.S. soybean prices, a large impending South American crop and a strengthening dollar will pressure exports, the USDA said.

Chinese imports of U.S. beans and meal have stagnated since late December due to problems at Chinese ports in moving out the large quantities imported that month. USDA said buying may resume soon after the Chinese New Year, but the imports will likely be from South America, whose prices for March-April delivery are significantly lower than U.S. prices.
